title: Irrationality of ∛3 via Eisenstein's Criterion
description: Proves ∛3 is irrational using Eisenstein's irreducibility criterion: X³-3 is Eisenstein at p=3, hence irreducible over ℤ, hence irreducible over ℚ (Gauss), hence has no rational roots, hence 3^(1/3) ∉ ℚ.

overview.historicalContext: Eisenstein's irreducibility criterion (1850) provides a powerful sufficient condition for a polynomial with integer coefficients to be irreducible. For f = X³ - 3, the prime p = 3 satisfies the criterion: 3 divides all non-leading coefficients (just the constant -3), 9 = 3² does not divide the constant term -3, and the leading coefficient 1 is not divisible by 3. Since X³ - 3 is also primitive (monic), Gauss's lemma extends irreducibility to ℚ[X]. An irreducible polynomial of degree ≥ 2 over ℚ has no rational roots, so ∛3 (a real root of X³ - 3) must be irrational.
overview.problemStatement: Can the Eisenstein criterion be used to give a structural algebraic proof that ∛3 is irrational, distinct from the direct counting argument?
overview.proofStrategy: Three steps: (1) Apply Eisenstein at p=3 to show X³-3 is irreducible over ℤ using Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion. (2) Use IsPrimitive.Int.irreducible_iff_irreducible_map_cast (Gauss's lemma) to transfer to ℚ[X]. (3) Show that an irreducible polynomial of degree ≥ 2 over ℚ has no rational roots; since ∛3 is a root of X³-3 and satisfies (3^(1/3))^3 = 3 via Real.rpow_mul, it must be irrational.

Gauss's lemma transfers irreducibility from ℤ[X] to ℚ[X] for primitive polynomials
